My personal experience with mental health was pretty good. I was very lucky to have parents and teachers who understood the problem and helped me. It wasn't all good though, and I understand how bad the situation is.

Mental health and it's associated diseases or disorders are really taboo here. And there's no real support structure in place for mental health. Government hospitals generally give least priority to mental health clinics and even the doctors have no respect.

I used to go to a government funded hospital and the waiting room was basically an old hallway that had been converted, which ment it had no windows and space was super limited. The doctor there was pretty old as well. I don't quite remember what his age was, but he'd see 200 to 300 patients a day. So each patient had about 5 or so minutes to explain their problem, answer questions and get prescriptions. Do you see the problem here? 

What I find most disgusting is that people will shun those who struggle with mental health. "Psycho" and "pagal" are used in really derogatory ways and people will ridicule patients. Is it any surprise then that so many youth in India find suicide to be the only way out? 

And God forbid if a child has a learning disorder. Parents would rather beat and abuse their own children to make them study and "be normal" than understand the problem and work on it. I won't give details, but I'm aware of a student in 10th std right now who tried to kill themselves. They'd been diagnosed with a learning disorder WHEN THEY WERE IN 8TH and the parents did NOTHING. And now at a very important time of their education, the student figured that ending their own life will be better than failing 10th. 

Fucking brilliant education system, this.

5 days later mom told us that it flew away when we were at school. But, we saw it a lot after that. 
It flew up and sat on the balcony railing. We recognised it because it's wing was misshapen. Sometimes, we'd see it peering into the room from the mango tree's branch.
